sections.title: 1. Acceptance
sections.text: By joining or using this server, its bot, or its tickets, you agree to these terms. If you don't agree, please leave the server.

sections.title: 2. Discord Rules
sections.text: You must follow Discord's Terms of Service and Community Guidelines at all times. You must be at least 13 years old, or the minimum age required in your country.

sections.title: 3. Respect Everyone
sections.text: No harassment, bullying, hate speech, discrimination, threats, or doxxing. Disagreements are fine, personal attacks are not.

sections.title: 4. Content
sections.text: No NSFW, gore, or illegal content. No malware, token loggers, scams, phishing links, or pirated material.

sections.title: 5. Spam & Advertising
sections.text: No spam, mass pings, or flooding. No advertising, self-promotion, or server invites (including by DM) without staff permission.

sections.title: 6. Bot Usage
sections.text: Don't abuse, exploit, or try to crash the bot. AI answers can be wrong, so don't rely on them for anything important, and don't use the bot to produce harmful content.

sections.title: 7. Tickets & Logs
sections.text: Tickets are private between you and staff. Staff can read them, and a transcript is saved to a staff-only log channel when a ticket closes. Don't open tickets to troll or spam.

sections.title: 8. Moderation
sections.text: Staff may warn, mute, kick, or ban at their discretion. Staff decisions are final, but you can appeal through a ticket. Using alt accounts to evade a ban results in a permanent ban.

sections.title: 9. Changes
sections.text: These terms may change at any time without notice. Continuing to use the server means you accept the current version.

sections.title: 1. Who this covers
sections.text: This policy covers the Risk Discord bot and its website. Risk is run by an individual, not a company. For any question or request below, use the support server linked on the website.

sections.title: 2. What Risk saves
sections.text: Risk saves only what its features need, tied to Discord user, server, channel and role IDs: coin balances, items and cooldowns (economy); XP, message counts and level settings (levels); per-server settings that admins choose, such as prefix, switched-off commands, auto-moderation and welcome messages; to-do lists, AFK notes and reminder text; warnings with the reason, moderator and time; welcome, log, ticket and sticky-message settings; and ticket records, including staff notes. Risk does not keep a copy of your general chat messages.

sections.title: 3. Messages Risk reads
sections.text: Risk reads messages in servers it is in so it can notice commands and count messages for levels. It saves the count, not the text. For the snipe commands it holds the last deleted and last edited message of each channel in memory only. These are replaced by newer ones and cleared when the bot restarts.

sections.title: 4. Tickets and server logs
sections.text: When a ticket closes, Risk posts a text transcript (messages, names and attachment links) to the staff log channel that server chose. Server logs post things like deleted and edited messages, joins and leaves, role, nickname and voice changes to the channel that server's admins choose. That content then lives in Discord, under that server's control. Risk itself keeps only the last 200 log summaries per server, in memory.

sections.title: 5. Outside services
sections.text: Some commands send what you type to other services to get an answer: AI questions go to Groq; weather locations to wttr.in; words to dictionaryapi.dev; QR text to qrserver.com; topics to Wikipedia; profile lookups to api.nerve.wtf and the platform being looked up; and GIF, image, joke, advice and trivia commands to nekos.best, waifu.pics, thecatapi.com, dog.ceo, randomfox.ca, icanhazdadjoke.com, adviceslip.com and opentdb.com. Don't send passwords or private details to these commands. Each service has its own policy.

sections.title: 6. The website
sections.text: The public pages show the bot's status and command list. They set no cookies, use no analytics or ads, and store nothing in your browser. Its host keeps ordinary request logs (IP address, time and page), and the pages load fonts from Google Fonts, which sees your IP address. The public status feed lists, for up to 30 servers the bot is in, the server's name, icon and member count. Server owners can ask to be left out.

sections.title: 7. The dashboard
sections.text: Signing in to the dashboard uses Discord's OAuth2. Risk asks for your Discord ID, name and avatar, and the list of servers you are in with your permissions there (the identify and guilds scopes). It uses these only to work out which servers you can manage, and asks Discord to revoke the access token right after sign-in. A random session cookie (HttpOnly, 6 hours) keeps you signed in, and the site holds your name, avatar and managed-server list in memory until you sign out, the session ends or the site restarts. Settings you save are stored with the bot like any other setting, and each save is noted in that server's logs with your name. If you change the bot's profile there, the picture, banner, name and bio you upload are sent to Discord for that server. Servers can also have a VIP status, stored as a server id with an optional end date.

sections.title: 8. How long data is kept
sections.text: Saved data stays on the bot's host until it is reset or deleted. Admins can reset XP with the level commands, clear warnings with the moderation commands, and you can clear your own to-do list. If Risk leaves a server, that server's saved data stays on the host until it is deleted on request.

sections.title: 9. Your choices
sections.text: You can ask what Risk has saved about you, or ask for it to be deleted, through the support server. Include your Discord user ID. Server admins can switch features off, exclude channels from XP and logs, or remove the bot. Removing the bot stops all collection from that server.

sections.title: 10. Sharing and security
sections.text: Risk does not sell your data or use it for advertising. It is shared only as described above, or when the law requires it. Saved files and secret keys are kept on the bot's host and not published, but no system is perfectly secure, so avoid putting sensitive information into any command.

sections.title: 11. Age
sections.text: Discord requires users to be at least 13, or the minimum age in their country. Risk is not meant for anyone younger and does not knowingly collect data from them.

sections.title: 12. Changes
sections.text: This policy may change as Risk gains features. The date at the bottom shows the latest version, and continuing to use Risk means you accept the current one.
